decorators.name: penv
decorators.doc: Links this schema to a cloud project, so `penv run` reads its values from there: `@penv=acme/api`. `@penv=<provider>:org/project` reads from another provider ([docs/PROVIDERS.md](https://github.com/penvhq/penvhq/blob/main/docs/PROVIDERS.md)). Without it, penv runs locally from the `.env` files beside the schema.

decorators.name: schema
decorators.doc: The grammar version this schema is written for, a whole number such as `@schema=1`. `.penv/config.toml` holds it now; a value here is still read.

decorators.name: defaultSensitive
decorators.doc: Whether a key that says nothing itself is masked: `@defaultSensitive=true` masks every key not marked `@sensitive=false`. A bundler-prefixed key (`NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_`, ...) is never sensitive by default.

decorators.name: defaultRequired
decorators.doc: Which keys need a value when they say nothing themselves. `@defaultRequired=true`: a key with no default needs one. `false`: no key does unless marked `@required`. `infer`: a key with a value in the schema is required.

decorators.name: currentEnv
decorators.doc: Names the key that holds the environment, used when neither `--env` nor `PENV_ENV` is set: `@currentEnv=$APP_ENV`. The `$` is optional.

decorators.name: import
decorators.doc: Reads the keys of another schema, so services share one definition: `@import(../.env.schema)`. Name keys after the path, `@import(../.env.schema, OPENAI_API_KEY)`, or with varlock's `pick=[OPENAI_API_KEY, DATABASE_URL]`, to take only those.

decorators.name: assert
decorators.doc: Evaluates an expression that must always be true, else `penv check` and `penv run` fail with the message: `@assert(startsWith($STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, "sk_"), "STRIPE_SECRET_KEY must start with sk_")`. Goes in the header or on a key; the last top-level comma starts the message.

decorators.name: type
decorators.doc: Checks the value before the command starts, so a malformed key fails at `penv check` rather than in the app. Constraints go in parentheses: `@type=string(startsWith=sk_)`, `number(min=1, max=10)`, `enum(development, production)`. An unknown type is checked as a string, with a warning.

decorators.name: required
decorators.doc: The key must have a value. `@required=forEnv(production)` needs one only in the environments named; `@required=false` is the same as `@optional`.

decorators.name: optional
decorators.doc: The key may be empty. `@optional=forEnv(development)` allows that only in the environments named; `@optional=false` is the same as `@required`.

decorators.name: sensitive
decorators.doc: Masks the value in the output of every `penv run`, as you want for `OPENAI_API_KEY`. `@sensitive=false` marks a value that may be shown. A bundler-prefixed key (`NEXT_PUBLIC_`, ...) cannot be sensitive, because its value ships to the browser.

decorators.name: example
decorators.doc: A sample value for people reading the schema: `@example=sk_test_fake`. penv never uses it as the value.

decorators.name: docs
decorators.doc: Where this key is documented, so the next person knows where to get one: `@docs=https://platform.openai.com/api-keys`.

decorators.name: deprecated
decorators.doc: Marks the key as on its way out, with an optional reason: `@deprecated="use DATABASE_URL"`. The key's hover says so.

decorators.name: dynamic
decorators.doc: The spec's marker for a value read at runtime. penv keeps it and does not act on it. It takes no value.

decorators.name: static
decorators.doc: The spec's marker for a value fixed at build time. penv keeps it and does not act on it. It takes no value.

decorators.name: hosts
decorators.doc: Seals the value: an agent's process holds a placeholder shaped by `@type`, and `penv run` puts the real value in only on the way to these hosts: `@hosts(api.openai.com)`. At most 32, with no scheme, port or path. A computed `@hosts=url($DATABASE_URL, host)` counts only where `[hosts]` in `.penv/config.toml` pins the same hosts; `penv check --pin-hosts` writes the pin.

decorators.name: rotate
decorators.doc: `penv check` reminds you to rotate the value once it is older than this: `@rotate=90d`. Units, largest first and each once: `y`, `m` (months), `w`, `d`, `h`, `min`, `s`, as in `1y6m`, `12h` or `30min`.

decorators.name: generateTypes
decorators.doc: varlock's. penv reads past it; `penv gen` writes typed files.

decorators.name: plugin
decorators.doc: varlock's. penv loads no plugins and warns; providers are compiled in.

decorators.name: redactLogs
decorators.doc: varlock's. penv reads past it; every `penv run` already masks sensitive values.

decorators.name: preventLeaks
decorators.doc: varlock's. penv reads past it.

decorators.name: envFlag
decorators.doc: varlock's older name for `@currentEnv`. penv reads past it; write `@currentEnv=$APP_ENV`.

decorators.name: setValuesBulk
decorators.doc: varlock's. penv reads past it.

decorators.name: disable
decorators.doc: varlock's. penv reads past it.

functions.name: ref
functions.doc: Another key's value, so a secret is written once: `ref(DATABASE_URL)`, or `${DATABASE_URL}` inside text. `${API_KEY:-dev-fake}` uses `dev-fake` when API_KEY is empty or unset; `${API_KEY-dev-fake}` only when it is unset.

functions.name: concat
functions.doc: Joins its arguments into one string: `concat("Bearer ", $API_KEY)`.

functions.name: fallback
functions.doc: The first argument that is not empty, for a key with a backup: `fallback($OPENAI_API_KEY, $API_KEY)`.

functions.name: if
functions.doc: `then` when the condition is true, otherwise `else` or empty: `if(forEnv(production), $STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, sk_test_fake)`. `false`, `0` and empty are false.

functions.name: eq
functions.doc: `true` when both arguments are the same text: `eq($APP_ENV, production)`.

functions.name: not
functions.doc: `true` when the argument is false, `0` or empty: `not(forEnv(production))`.

functions.name: forEnv
functions.doc: `true` when the current environment is one of those named: `forEnv(staging, production)`.

functions.name: penv
functions.doc: A value read from the provider, so one key can borrow another environment's: `penv(production/DATABASE_URL)`. `env/KEY` uses the `@penv=` project; `penv()` reads this key from the current environment. The address is written, never computed; `exec()` is refused, since a schema never runs a shell command.

functions.name: match
functions.doc: The value of the case whose label equals the subject, `_` when none does: `match($APP_ENV, production: api.example.com, _: localhost)`. With no match and no `_`, it fails.

functions.name: and
functions.doc: `true` when every argument is true: `and(forEnv(production), not(isEmpty($STRIPE_SECRET_KEY)))`.

functions.name: or
functions.doc: `true` when any argument is true: `or(forEnv(staging), forEnv(production))`.

functions.name: startsWith
functions.doc: `true` when the value starts with the prefix: `startsWith($STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, "sk_live_")`.

functions.name: endsWith
functions.doc: `true` when the value ends with the suffix: `endsWith($DATABASE_URL, "sslmode=require")`.

functions.name: random
functions.doc: Random characters for a local secret nobody types: `random(length=32)`. `penv run` generates it once and keeps it in this machine's `.env.local`. `length` is 8 to 512 and required, except for `kind=uuid`, which takes none.
functions.subject: none

functions.name: url
functions.doc: Reads one part of a URL, or writes parts and returns the whole URL, so a host is never copied by hand: `url($DATABASE_URL, host)`, `url($DATABASE_URL, port=6543)`. A call reads or writes, never both; a written `password=` is a `$KEY`. As a pipe step: `${DATABASE_URL | url(host)}`.
functions.subject: required

functions.name: json
functions.doc: Reads a field of a JSON document, or writes fields and returns compact JSON: `json($APP_CONFIG, db.host)`. A path is `a.b[0]`, `["a.b"]` or `a["x.y"].c`; with no subject, writing starts from `{}`. As a pipe step: `${APP_CONFIG | json(db.host)}`.
functions.subject: optional

functions.name: hash
functions.doc: `hash($API_KEY, algo=sha256, length=8)` gives a short fingerprint of a key, so you can tell which key a machine has without showing it. The same inputs always give the same result; `hmac-*` needs `key=$KEY`. As a pipe step: `${API_KEY | hash(algo=sha256)}`.
functions.subject: required

args.name: algo
args.doc: The digest or HMAC to compute: `algo=sha256`.

args.name: encoding
args.doc: How the result is written; `hex` when left out.

args.name: length
args.doc: Keeps the first N characters of the encoded result, at least 1: `length=8`.

args.name: key
args.doc: The secret an `hmac-*` algorithm signs with: `key=$WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Refused for a plain digest.

functions.name: raw
functions.doc: Embeds JSON that already exists as a `json()` option value, parsed rather than quoted as text: `json(db=raw($DB_CONFIG))`. Fails when the value is not valid JSON.

filters.name: urlencode
filters.doc: Percent-encodes the value so it is safe inside a URL, such as a password holding `@`: `postgres://app:${DB_PASSWORD | urlencode}@db.example.com/app`. Steps chain left to right.

filters.name: base64
filters.doc: The value in standard base64, for a header that expects it: `${API_KEY | base64}`.

filters.name: trim
filters.doc: The value without surrounding whitespace, for a key pasted with a stray newline: `${OPENAI_API_KEY | trim}`.

filters.name: b64d
filters.doc: Decodes standard base64: `${GOOGLE_CREDENTIALS_B64 | b64d}`. A value that is not base64 fails.

algorithms.name: hmac-sha256
algorithms.doc: HMAC with SHA-256, signed with `key=`: `hash($PAYLOAD, algo=hmac-sha256, key=$WEBHOOK_SECRET)`.

algorithms.name: hmac-sha512
algorithms.doc: HMAC with SHA-512, signed with `key=`: `hash($PAYLOAD, algo=hmac-sha512, key=$WEBHOOK_SECRET)`.

url-parts.name: host
url-parts.doc: The host, such as `db.example.com`. A URL that names several hosts fails.

url-parts.name: port
url-parts.doc: The port, such as `5432`; empty when the URL has none.

url-parts.name: origin
url-parts.doc: Scheme, host and port, such as `https://api.example.com`. Read only.

url-parts.name: password
url-parts.doc: The password. Always sensitive; to write one, give a `$KEY` reference, never a literal.

random-kinds.name: uuid
random-kinds.doc: A version-4 UUID; takes no length.

types.name: string
types.doc: Any text. Constraints: `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `matches`, as in `string(startsWith=sk_, minLength=20)`.

args.name: startsWith
args.doc: The value must start with this text: `string(startsWith=sk_live_)`.

args.name: endsWith
args.doc: The value must end with this text: `string(endsWith=.example.com)`.

args.name: minLength
args.doc: The value must have at least this many characters: `string(minLength=32)`.

args.name: maxLength
args.doc: The value must have at most this many characters: `string(maxLength=64)`.

args.name: matches
args.doc: A regular expression kept for the generated code and the cloud; penv warns that it does not check values against it: `string(matches=^sk_[a-z]+$)`.

types.name: number
types.doc: A number. Constraints: `min`, `max`, `isInt`, `precision`; a whole number is `number(isInt=true)`.

args.name: min
args.doc: The value must be this number or more: `number(min=1)`.

args.name: max
args.doc: The value must be this number or less: `number(max=100)`.

args.name: precision
args.doc: Decimal places kept for the generated code and the cloud; penv warns that it does not check values against it: `number(precision=2)`.

types.name: boolean
types.doc: `true` or `false`; `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `1` and `0` also pass, in any case.

types.name: url
types.doc: An absolute URL: a scheme, `://` and a host, such as `postgres://db.example.com/app`.

types.name: port
types.doc: A TCP port, 1 to 65535. Constraints: `min`, `max`, as in `port(min=1024)`.

args.name: min
args.doc: The lowest port allowed: `port(min=1024)` refuses the privileged ports.

types.name: enum
types.doc: One of the members listed: `enum(development, staging, production)`. A quoted member may hold `=`.

environments.name: development
environments.doc: What penv runs when no `--env`, `PENV_ENV` or `@currentEnv` key names an environment. It reads `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.development` and `.env.development.local`. With `@penv=` set and the cloud out of reach, development runs on this machine's files when they hold values; every other environment fails.

environments.name: staging
environments.doc: `penv run --env staging` reads `.env.staging` and `.env.staging.local` over `.env` and `.env.local`, and `forEnv(staging)` is true.

environments.name: production
environments.doc: `penv run --env production` reads `.env.production` and `.env.production.local` over `.env` and `.env.local`, and `forEnv(production)` is true: `@required=forEnv(production)` needs the key there only.

environments.name: test
environments.doc: `penv run --env test` reads `.env`, `.env.test` and `.env.test.local`, and skips `.env.local`. A `random()` value generated for a test run is kept in `.env.test.local`.

reference-forms.name: $KEY
reference-forms.doc: Another key's value, in a function argument or inside text: `postgres://db.example.com/$DB_NAME`. Write `\$` for a literal dollar sign.

reference-forms.name: ${KEY}
reference-forms.doc: Another key's value, with braces so text can follow the name: `https://${API_HOST}:8443`.

reference-forms.name: ${KEY:-default}
reference-forms.doc: The key's value, or the default when the key is empty or unset: `${AWS_REGION:-us-east-1}`.

reference-forms.name: ${KEY-default}
reference-forms.doc: The key's value, or the default only when the key is unset; an empty value stays empty: `${LOG_LEVEL-info}`.

reference-forms.name: ${KEY | filter}
reference-forms.doc: The value run through each step, left to right: `${DB_PASSWORD | urlencode}`, `${DATABASE_URL | url(host)}`.
